tips.comment: Finished a decent 2nd on good ground in a Class 6 event. Drops back into a Class 6 event after two recent runs in Class 3 events. Likely to run well in easy company.
In A Hurry looks the best bet here. The opening mark looks pretty lenient given recent form. Finished in the top two in 4 of 5 previous starts. Should get close on handicap debut.

Lady Winalong had her first run on turf for almost a year recently and performed with credit. This 6-year-old mare has had her best form on A/W tracks but likes firm ground and will probably enjoy a different challenge.
Taken a while to get going this season but best effort so far when 2nd at Musselburgh last week. Lurking on a dangerous mark so should run very well.

Rain Cap has won 4 times here at Catterick. His last win was course and distance back in July 23, and he is off a 1lb lower mark here. He has been placed in 3 of his 6 starts this season, including when 4th of 18 at Thirsk last week when he was beaten by less than 2 lengths. He looks like a good EW bet based on his excellent course form.

Myboymax finished four lengths behind Cosmic Soul over course and distance a month ago when they were 5th and 2nd. But he got outpaced that time and on four pounds better terms could reverse that form against his locally trained rival.

This R Varian-trained 3-year-old filly improved from her racecourse debut to only be beaten 1 1/4 lengths in second of the eight runners behind the highly regarded A M Balding-trained Blue Bolt over one mile on good ground at Newbury. With retained jockey Jim Crowley in the saddle, it looks like a win today.

I like the jockey switch here for a horse that has on several occasions failed to settle for other jockeys. That could well be the key, and despite failing to settle, the horse has some form in the book that's good enough to go close off this mark anyway. He was beaten less than a length in his only other run over C&D, and breeding suggests that he's well worth a first try on this softer ground since many of the sire's progeny really acted well on it.
Dual winner last season who took a step forward from reappearance when 3rd at Leicester last time. Up a lb for that, so needs a bit more but should still run well in this weak race.

MC'TED looks worth an each way interest for 3 places in this runner race at the 16/1 currently on offer with Bet365. He has a great record over C&D with form figures reading 12261 and he has also dropped to 4lb below his last winning mark. For a much more detailed write-up please see my X feed.

Daughter of Bated Breath & If So ( Dam's sire Ifraaj ) who was last seen at Goodwood 26 days ago where finishing a creditable 4th/10 steps up in trip here racing over the 7 furlong trip for the first time here that being a good move by her connections as this new trip can bring out further improvement and she is open to plenty of progress still and after six career starts she is most certainly ready to tackle this trip which is well worth exploring currently operating on a mark of 69 J R Fanshawe's inmate looks poised to get competitive here especially with a good analysis of this class 5 handicap clearly showing So Sassy will be well suited in a race of this nature with an ideal pace level likely to play well into her strengths here at the Yarmouth track jockey Jack Doughty takes the ride and can give So Sassy a promising ride here at Yarmouth merits consideration

Returned from a 308-day break and showed bags of improvement for it with a 4th here when running out of turf to catch the front three after settling at the back. Was 2nd here the next time around and more recently at Chelmsford by a nose. The potential is there.

Sea of Kings was beaten when odds-on favorite last time in a lowly maiden at Chepstow in May. But that race looks a lot hotter than at first glance. The two who beat him that day look a bit special, and Chepstow can be challenging for a lot of runners. It is a niche track, a bit like Marmite.

This W J Haggas-trained 3-year-old colt has finished second in his first two races. The latest was over one mile on good ground at Doncaster 33 days ago when staying on well in the closing stages to only be beaten 3/4 length in second of the 16 runners behind the C Appleby-trained King's Charter. With Cieren Fallon back onboard, he can make it third time lucky tonight.

Won classified race here over CD on good to soft 9 days ago by 7.5L. Despite carrying extra today, has a good chance to follow up for trainer J Candish, whose string has been in form over the last month.

Charles Fort is a 2-year-old son of St. Mark's Basilica ex Archangel Gabriel, thus a half-brother to Ville de Grace by Le Havre. He'll be ridden by W Lordan for Aidan O'Brien & Coolmore. He's drawn 6/10. He may be one for your horse tracker. He makes his racecourse debut here in this 6f maiden.. His sire may become the leading first-season sire for Coolmore this season. I make him my nap of the day.
Day Trader looks good value here. Longer trip will suit. Looks on a good mark on French flat form. Won a maiden hurdle last time out and looks to follow up here.

Nicola Burns is booked for the first time here, and she actually has a better strike rate than the pro jockey she replaces. So the fact that she claims 7lb is a serious bonus, especially since the horse has gone close when placed twice in big handicaps this year. She was only beaten a head in the first of those two runs, and the horses around her would put her nearer the 78 mark than the 72 she races off here. The first-time hood and the jockey's claim add extra weight to the case, and she could go very close.

Low numbers have a big advantage here, and Masked Angel in stall 3 appeals at a massive 33/1. She has dropped to a very good-looking mark, and the ground has come into her favor. She ran better than her finishing position suggests here over an inadequate trip.
